newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - March 14.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - March 14.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Friday morning:
** Petro-chemical major Reliance Industries Ltd has broken its 20-year old honeymoon by paying 500 million rupees as income tax for the financial year 1996/97, the daily Economic Times reports.
The payment also ends its status as one of the biggest zero-tax companies in the country, the paper says.
** The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has stepped up dollar buying to arrest the Indian rupee's gain on the back of a rise in foreign direct and portfolio investment, bank dealers said on Thursday.
Unlike in the past, there was no nervous dollar covering preceding the budget presentation on February 28, dealers said.

** Former Reserve Bank deputy governor and capital account convertibitlity panel chairman SS Tarapore has ruled out the possibility of softening of interest rates in the medium term, the Financial Express says.
The paper quoted Tarapore as cautioning the industry against expecting any reduction in lending rates.

** The Indian rupee opened steady at 35.845/850 against the dollar on Friday, dealers said. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and an influential state-run commercial bank expected to buy dollars to siphon off excess of dollar supply in the market.
** Blue-chip shares at major Indian bourses nudged lower in lacklustre trade on Thursday as fresh demand slowed, traders said.
** The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange fell 7.86 points, or 0.21 percent, to close at 3754.51.
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index dropped 7.70 points, or 0.72 percent to 1066.50.
** The Delhi share index lost 4.13 points to 772.58.
** The Calcutta share index slumped 3.26 points to 459.81.
** The Madras share index was up 30.92 points to 3,570.26.
